Time Series is a series of values organized by time [Ch. 5]. It involves recording events over time, whether regularly or sporadically [Ch. 5]. Time-series databases are optimized for handling such data, especially in scenarios involving high-velocity data volumes from IoT, event logs, and other use cases [Ch. 5]. These databases often use memory buffering to support fast writes and reads [Ch. 5]. Measurement data in time series is generated regularly, such as from temperature or air-quality sensors, while event-based data is irregular and created every time an event occurs, like a motion sensor detecting movement [Ch. 5].

It involves running batches of data every few seconds to every few minutes, depending on the use case and performance requirements [Ch. 8].
